eyebrow: Eat like the locals in Prachinburi · Updated 2026
intro: Prachinburi is a province where great food doesn't need to cost much — from legendary noodles that have been selling beside the train tracks for over half a century to fresh river fish straight from the Bang Pakong. We've pulled together 10 restaurants that locals here actually eat at and travelers keep recommending, covering everything from savory mains and desserts to charming riverside cafés.
chips: 🐟 River fish along the Bang Pakong

blocks.html:
If there's one thing Prachinburi people are proudest of, it's the food. The Bang Pakong and Prachinburi rivers running through the province mean riverside restaurants and fresh river fish are everywhere — sit down, order grilled prawns and fresh-water fish tom yum, and let the cool breeze do the rest. The Dong Khi Lek strip along the old Highway 33 has become a boat noodle destination where passing drivers always pull over, and out in Kabin Buri and Ban Sang you'll find local restaurants that have been feeding the same families for generations. Prachinburi food is a blend of home-style cooking made with care and fresh ingredients pulled straight from the rivers and gardens around town.

Several restaurants on this list have a story worth telling. Mae Buay noodles in Ban Sang started as a tiny wooden stall beside the railway station nearly 60 years ago — today the founder's son runs a full restaurant with air-conditioning and the same recipe intact. Khrua A-Ku in Kabin Buri is a Thai restaurant so consistently packed it tops the province's most-recommended lists. Khrua Jao Khun Thor has made its name with a giant straw-grilled snakehead that everyone orders without thinking. And for those who just want to sit quietly with a coffee by the water, 93 Degrees Coffee and Craftel Cafe — a charming train-carriage-themed café — are both worth stopping for. Pick your favourite and go taste it.

blocks.name: Mae Buay Noodles (Ku Na)
blocks.signature: Pork noodles old-school recipe, slow-simmered pork-bone broth, tamarind-roasted pad thai, khao kha moo, steamed buns
blocks.descHtml:
Ask anyone driving through Ban Sang district where to eat noodles and almost every answer points to "Mae Buay" — known locally as Ku Na's shop. This restaurant has been part of Ban Sang for over 60 years, starting as a small wooden shelter beside the canal near the train station back in 1964. Today the founder's son, Ku Na, runs an expanded shop along the main road near the Wat Ban Sang intersection, with comfortable air-conditioned seating. It's the kind of place suited to a first meal of the day on the road, or a family wanting to sit down for a relaxed lunch.

The star of the shop is the pork noodles with an old-school recipe: the broth is made by slow-simmering pork bones with vegetables for hours until it's naturally sweet and rounded, with almost no MSG needed. Regulars say you can drink the broth plain and it's already delicious. The homemade condiments on the table — chili powder and pickled chili vinegar — are made in-house too. Another big seller is the pad thai, which gets its sour-sweet depth from tamarind sauce that's been roasted in-house. For something more filling, there's braised pork leg with tender meat, pork blood soup, and leng saep. The steamed buns are a known take-home souvenir that people always carry out.

Prices are very approachable — noodles start in the mid-tens of baht, portions generous for a local restaurant. That's why this is a place people have been eating since their parents' generation and come back again with their children. The kind of loyalty that spans decades doesn't come by luck — it comes from keeping the original recipe and passing the care down through the family.

Good to know: the restaurant opens at 7am and closes at 4pm daily. Late morning through noon gets busy, especially on weekends. If you want a quieter experience, arrive earlier. Parking is easy along the Ban Sang–Train Station road near the Wat Ban Sang intersection.
mustOrder: Pad thai with house-roasted tamarind sauce
blocks.bestFor: First meal of the day on the road — great for families
blocks.spice: Self-adjust (house-made chili powder / pickled chili vinegar)
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: pork leg rice · User:Bi89 / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 3.0)

blocks.name: Khrua A-Ku Kabin Buri
blocks.signature: Deep-fried pork belly, nam prik khai pu (crab-roe chili relish), deep-fried sea bass in fish sauce, stir-fried king oyster mushrooms with fresh prawns, kaeng som cha-om kai
blocks.descHtml:
Khrua A-Ku is the go-to Thai restaurant in Kabin Buri — almost anyone driving the 304 Kabin–Korat highway knows it. Situated on the Kabin Buri–Pak Thong Chai road near the Ban Khok Udom intersection, the restaurant is an open-air space built from natural wood, shaded by large trees, with plenty of parking. Works equally well for families stopping en route, friend groups, and tour buses — the kitchen takes large table-booking orders and makes box lunches too. For anyone looking for their first proper meal in the province or a serious dinner anywhere near Kabin, this is the name people mention first.

The dishes reviewers come back to most consistently: nam prik khai pu (crab-roe chili relish) — many describe it as perfectly balanced, sweet-sour-salty-spicy, wonderful to eat with fresh vegetables. Kaeng som cha-om kai brings bold, homey heat. Deep-fried pork belly has crisp skin and tender meat. Deep-fried sea bass in fish sauce comes in a large piece. Stir-fried king oyster mushrooms with fresh prawns gives you the crunch of the mushrooms and sweetness of the prawns together. For those wanting serious heat, the kaeng lueang bamboo shoot with prawns gets described as deep-spicy and satisfying.

Prices run 101–250 THB per person — stir-fries start at around 100 THB, larger fish dishes scale up by size. Fair value for the freshness and portions. Open daily approximately 10:30–22:00. One common observation in reviews: dishes are cooked fresh to order, so expect some wait during busy periods — calling ahead 20–30 minutes if you're on a schedule makes the visit smoother.

What keeps Khrua A-Ku at the top of Prachinburi Thai food rankings is consistency: fresh ingredients, home-kitchen flavors that don't tire, and a location that's easy to pull into when you're passing through. Both locals and road-trippers rely on it.
mustOrder: Nam prik khai pu (crab-roe chili relish)
Deep-fried sea bass in fish sauce
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province / roadstop on Highway 304 / groups
blocks.spice: Some dishes are seriously spicy (kaeng lueang / kaeng som) — adjustable

blocks.name: Baan Rim Nam
blocks.signature: Grilled river prawns, fresh-water fish tom yum, tod man pla krai, yam pla duk fu
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Prachinburi and want a big riverside meal at a place locals call their go-to restaurant for the province, "Baan Rim Nam" is one of the first names anyone mentions. The restaurant sits on the Prachinburi River along Highway 3069 (Prachin–Si Maha Phot road), only about 500 metres past Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Hospital — easy to find. The standout is multi-level seating that steps down toward the riverbank — get the lowest tier for the full river breeze experience, fish drifting past below the table. Works well for families treating elders, or groups who want a long, relaxed meal. Both open-air riverside seating and air-conditioned rooms are available.

The heroes of the menu are the river dishes. Grilled river prawns — large, firm, eaten with a sharp seafood dipping sauce — are the most mentioned item in reviews. Fresh-water fish follows: tod yum pla khao (fresh-water fish tom yum), yam pla duk fu (crispy puffed catfish salad), and tod man pla krai (bouncy river fish cakes). Those who want game-style dishes can try that too. For larger groups, sea bass fried in fish sauce, morning glory stir-fry with crispy pork, and hor mok (banana-leaf steamed curry) are all popular shared dishes. Reviewers consistently praise the fresh ingredients, bold yam flavors (sour-sweet-salty-spicy through), and how quickly food arrives with generous portions.

Prices are genuinely friendly — averaging about 101–250 THB per person. Whole fish dishes range roughly 110–350 THB by size. A small group eating comfortably runs 600–700 THB altogether. Free Wi-Fi, parking, card accepted, and pets welcome. Open daily 10:00–22:00, both lunch and dinner.

Small note: the open-air riverside zone sometimes has flies as expected at a waterfront restaurant, and weekends can mean waiting for a table. Arriving before peak hours or calling ahead helps. Overall it's a restaurant that delivers both river views and fresh-water seafood at prices that don't sting — which is exactly why both locals and tourists come back.
mustOrder: Tod yum pla khao (fresh-water fish tom yum)
blocks.bestFor: Family or group meal — long riverside lunch or dinner
blocks.spice: Medium–spicy (yam / tom yum dishes are quite hot)
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: tom yum · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.name: Khrua Chalawan
blocks.signature: Pork belly with fish sauce on rice, fresh seafood cooked to order, firm prawns, fresh squid
blocks.descHtml:
Khrua Chalawan is a made-to-order Thai restaurant in central Prachinburi town — a place locals like to meet for both lunch and dinner. It's all about fresh, homestyle cooking: every dish made to order, bold flavors that go perfectly with hot steamed rice. For anyone driving through the city wanting a simple, filling, affordable meal, this is the name Prachinburi locals tend to think of first. Works for families, groups of friends, and larger tables.

The dish many people order is the pork belly with fish sauce on rice — crispy skin on the outside, tender inside, tossed in a sweet-salty fish sauce. Seafood lovers are also well served: the kitchen focuses on freshness, with firm prawns and fresh squid stir-fried or made into tom yum with a rounded, satisfying flavor. Beyond these, there are local Prachinburi specialties like bai liang pad khai (local vegetable stir-fried with egg) and tom yum with kai krai thong — a local egg variety — which is a provincial specialty not to miss. Multiple reviewers agree across the board that nearly every dish is good, ingredients are fresh, and the plating shows more care than your average made-to-order shop.

Air-conditioned seating, friendly service, convenient parking, and delivery available for those ordering to take home. Prices around 100–250 THB per person — good value for what you get. This consistency over the years is exactly why the restaurant has a loyal regular following.

Located at 14–16 Prachin Takham 3 Road, near Prachinburi municipality. Easy to find, central. Open from mid-morning through the evening, approximately 11:00–22:00. Peak lunch and dinner hours on weekends can be busy — call ahead to reserve a table for larger groups.
mustOrder: Pork belly with fish sauce on rice
Fresh prawns and squid cooked to order
blocks.bestFor: Family meal or evening dinner with friends in town
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: seafood · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.name: Khrua Jao Khun Thor
blocks.signature: Straw-grilled snakehead fish, thick sea bass tom yum, phad cha, coconut jelly / fresh tofu pudding
blocks.descHtml:
Khrua Jao Khun Thor is a grilled-fish restaurant on Suwannasorn Road, about 2 km from the Naresuan roundabout — the kind of bold Thai restaurant that both Prachinburi locals and people stopping on the way to Khao Yai name first. The restaurant is an open pavilion with long wooden tables, a large parking area, and a cool breeze through the space. No dress code, relaxed atmosphere, exactly right for a family or group who wants a proper shared meal.

The restaurant's hero dish is the straw-grilled snakehead fish — a large fish, arm-sized, grilled over straw until it develops a straw-smoke fragrance, with firm, sweet flesh. Several reviews note the meat is "perfectly dry, not oily, more enjoyable than salt-grilled fish." Second most ordered is the thick sea bass tom yum — served hot, deeply flavored, with chunky boneless fish pieces, consistently described as fresh and vibrant. For those who want stir-fries there's phad cha, phad cha with pepper, and stir-fried vegetables with fish sauce. Finish with cooling desserts: coconut jelly, fresh tofu pudding (tau hua nom sod), and fresh-milk pudding, all of which help cut through the heat.

The overall flavors lean bold and traditional Thai — those who enjoy spice will have a great time. Prices are genuinely accessible: most dishes 70–200 THB, the straw-grilled snakehead around 235 THB. Most reviews praise the generous portions and fast service. Open daily approximately 10:00–22:00. One minor observation from reviews: the open pavilion setting means flies during lunch (typical for grilled-fish restaurants), but evenings are cool and comfortable for a long meal. If you're in Prachinburi and want fresh-grilled snakehead fish in the hands of a proper Thai kitchen, this is the address to mark.

blocks.name: Lek-Was Som Tam Nong Juang
blocks.signature: Som tam with fermented fish sauce, grilled chicken, grilled beef, sun-dried beef, tam sua, sweet liver
blocks.descHtml:
Ask anyone in the Nong Juang area of Prachinburi where to go for som tam and "Lek-Was Som Tam Nong Juang" comes up immediately. A small Isan restaurant with an orange roof on the roadside in the Dong Khi Lek area near Wat Nong Juang, where generations of regulars have eaten for over 15 years. The standout point people keep mentioning: the restaurant uses properly cooked fermented fish sauce (pla ra) in every dish, which gives the som tam a deep, complex, well-rounded savory-sour-spicy flavor that stays with you — proper Isan, not a toned-down version. Works for workers, families, and passing drivers wanting a satisfying lunch.

The must-order is the som tam with fermented fish sauce paired with grilled chicken, followed by the grilled meats: grilled beef and sun-dried beef (or sun-dried pork) that reviews describe as properly dry and fragrant with herbs, excellent dipped in the spicy sauce. If you want something more adventurous, the tam sua and chicken-feet tam are here. Sweet liver (tap wan) rounds out the table and is another dish that brings people back. There's a full spread of Isan dishes — som tam varieties, laab, nam tok, soups, and grilled items — easy to make a shared table out of.

The atmosphere is a warm, local shop — not fancy, but clean and welcoming. The owner is friendly and chatty, prepares fresh ingredients visibly in front of you, and there's even a signature som tam mural on the front wall to photograph. Prices accessible: most dishes under 100 THB. Spice level adjustable to preference.

Open daily during the daytime, approximately 09:00–15:30 — it closes relatively early. If you're planning a lunch, build in extra time. During busy periods you may wait a bit; calling ahead or ordering in advance makes the visit easier. A long-established som tam shop endorsed by locals for years — anyone passing through Prachinburi who wants proper Isan food made by a real cook should mark this one.
mustOrder: Som tam with fermented fish sauce
blocks.bestFor: Midday Isan lunch with bold flavors — good for groups and families
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: som tam · Vyacheslav Argenberg / Wikimedia (CC BY 4.0)

blocks.name: Nai Tin Boat Noodles (Prachinburi Branch)
blocks.area: Mueang Prachinburi (old Highway 33, Dong Khi Lek sub-district), Prachinburi Province
blocks.signature: Pork / beef boat noodles, rich dense broth, braised beef with kaphrao, moo krajet
blocks.descHtml:
Driving into Prachinburi along the old Highway 33 near Dong Khi Lek sub-district and feeling your stomach grumble? Nai Tin Boat Noodles, Prachinburi branch, is the address to pin. This branch carries the original recipe from the founder "Khun Tin," who started out near Lam Luk Ka Canal 3 and brought the recipe to Prachinburi, where it's become a favourite with both locals and passing drivers. Works especially well for a late morning through afternoon meal — easy to pair with a visit to Wang Bo waterfall or the Dong Khi Lek area nearby.

The hero of the shop is the boat noodles — both pork and beef versions. What reviewers consistently praise is the dense, intensely flavored broth that needs no extra seasoning, with the authentic aromatic depth of a proper boat noodle shop. Braised pork and braised beef are tender and perfectly done. Noodles cooked just right — not soggy. Firm fish balls. The moo krajet (glazed pork slices) are made fresh daily and pleasant to snack on. But the dish that many say steals the show is the braised beef kaphrao — the beef is practically melting, stir-fried with a punchy flavor that pairs perfectly with hot steamed rice. Finish with desserts like sticky rice with fresh milk, or fried banana.

Very wallet-friendly — boat noodles start at 20 THB a bowl. Getting multiple bowls in the classic boat-noodle style is easy on the budget. Relaxed atmosphere, no dress code, works equally well solo, as a family, or as a road stop. To avoid the midday queue (11:30–13:00), try arriving slightly earlier or later.

Open daily approximately 08:30–16:00, though some days there may be closures — check the restaurant's Facebook page before heading out. Located on the old Highway 33, easy to find and with good parking. For a tasty bowl of boat noodles in Prachinburi at an honest price, this shop is the uncomplicated answer.
blocks.bestFor: Morning to afternoon road stop — budget boat noodles
blocks.hours: 08:30–16:00 daily (some days may close — check the page first)

blocks.name: 93 Degrees Coffee
blocks.signature: Riverside coffee, smooth-tasting drinks, Bang Pakong river view
blocks.descHtml:
93 Degrees Coffee (full name: Ninety Three Degrees Coffee) is a riverside café in central Prachinburi, tucked on Kaeo Phichit Road directly along the main river of the city — a short drive from the old town. It's a place for anyone wanting to escape the bustle and sit quietly with a coffee, catching the river breeze. Good for those who enjoy nature atmospheres, solo work sessions, long-stay groups, or friends meeting up. The space is clearly zoned: air-conditioned indoor rooms and a garden area along the river with a constant breeze. Multiple photo spots throughout — wooden walkways, lush greenery, and a river backdrop that photographs well from almost every angle.

The drink reviewers mention most is the Americano Pineapple — a cold Americano with fresh pineapple pieces floating on top, the tangy-sweet fruit cutting against the coffee in a refreshing way. For sweeter tastes, caramel milk and cocoa are both described as creamy and not overly sweet. For something sparkling, there's a mint chocolate cold coffee that delivers a clean mint fragrance. To close, homemade baked goods made fresh daily include Basque cheesecake and a smooth cheesecake — both get positive mentions. Drink prices are mostly under 100 THB — reasonable for the setting and river views.

Reviews consistently point in the same direction: calm riverside atmosphere, cool and shaded, a good mental reset with easy-drinking coffee. Pastries and cake are also well-received. This combination makes it one of the cafés that both Prachinburi residents and café-hopping visitors keep returning to — a riverside café in the middle of town is genuinely rare.

Good to know: open Tue–Fri 08:00–17:00, Sat–Sun 09:00–17:00, closed Mondays. Closes relatively early, so better suited to morning through afternoon than an evening visit. Parking can be limited at busy periods — riverside-view seats fill fast on weekends. Pets welcome, free Wi-Fi, card payments accepted.
blocks.bestFor: Café lovers wanting a quiet river-view sit — morning to afternoon
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: café · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.name: Craftel Cafe
blocks.area: Si Maha Phot District, Prachinburi Province
blocks.signature: Coffee, rich cold cocoa, bakery, train-carriage themed décor
blocks.descHtml:
Drive through the Khlong Rang Sai Nai area of Si Maha Phot and you'll spot a shop decorated as if a full train carriage was parked across from the 7-Eleven — that's Craftel Cafe, a café that has become a go-to stop for both Prachinburi locals and people driving through to the 304 Industrial Estate. The interior is a committed train-carriage theme: warm brown wood tones, vintage red seat cushions, replica windows that make you feel like you're riding a European train with a Japanese minimalist edge. Every corner is photogenic. Works for café-hoppers, couples, friend groups, or anyone wanting a quiet table to work.

The drink that gets the most mentions is the matcha strawberry latte — green matcha layers against pink strawberry, visually irresistible, with a gentle matcha fragrance balancing the sweet-tart strawberry. Coffee drinkers are well served with Americano, latte, and cold-brew options. For something sweet and rich, the cold cocoa is described as "just the right intensity." The bakery side rotates daily-made cakes and sourdough bread. Real reviewers consistently say: "cake is good, coffee is solid, the shop is beautifully designed, and the staff are genuinely warm and friendly."

Prices run about 101–250 THB per person — fair for a café with this level of atmosphere. Open Tue–Sun 08:00–17:00, closed Mondays (except public holidays). Spacious parking beside the shop. One thing to know: the café has been trending on social media, so weekends bring crowds. If you want a comfortable photo corner, mid-morning or late afternoon on a weekday is your best bet. A café that delivers on food, atmosphere, and seating — works equally as a road-trip stop or a friend meet-up.
blocks.bestFor: Café-hoppers wanting a photogenic sit with friends

blocks.name: Mesa Singha Boat Noodles
blocks.signature: Dense boat noodles — pork / beef, full toppings
blocks.descHtml:
Mesa Singha Boat Noodles is a boat noodle shop on the old Highway 33 that many people spot from the road — intrigued by the name — and pull in for a try, only to return every time they pass through Prachinburi after that. A great fit for anyone looking for a comfortable midday meal on the way to Khao Yai or Khao E-To, equally welcoming for families, couples, or solo diners. The hero of the shop is the dense boat noodle broth with honey-marinated pork and herb-braised beef — full toppings of fish balls, innards, and fresh vegetables.

The dish people keep ordering is the herb-braised beef boat noodles — the broth carries a light herbal fragrance from the slow-braised beef that many reviewers say "tastes complete on its own, no seasoning needed." Honey-marinated pork is tender and gently sweet. Another dish the shop is known for is pork satay on large skewers — juicy meat, fragrant from the grill, paired with the dipping sauce and cucumber relish that many reviewers specifically call out as a must-order. Also available: pork wontons, crispy pork cracklings, rice dishes, and a tea-coffee bar to close the meal.

The atmosphere is open-air with wooden tables, and the feature many people enjoy most is the garden seating area beside the shop under large trees — open, airy, cool breeze throughout. Large parking lot makes it a natural road-trip rest stop. Prices around 100–200 THB per person — good value for the quality and portions. This combination has kept the shop highly rated and continuously mentioned in Prachinburi food groups.

Good to know: open 09:00–17:30 daily — closes relatively early, so midday through early afternoon is the right window. Located on the old Highway 33 near the Hatari factory in Dong Khi Lek, slightly outside the town center. Pin it on your map before setting out, as the road moves quickly and it's easy to overshoot.
blocks.bestFor: Midday road-stop meal on the way to Khao Yai

blocks.title: What to know before you eat in Prachinburi

items.title: A car is the most practical option
items.text: Several of the best restaurants are outside the town center or in different districts altogether — Ban Sang, Kabin Buri, and Dong Khi Lek. Renting a car or using a private transfer is by far the most flexible option, since Grab coverage in Prachinburi is thin and public transport rarely reaches the roadside spots.

items.title: Always carry cash
items.text: Most noodle shops, som tam stalls, and roadside restaurants accept cash or PromptPay bank transfer only — card payments are almost nonexistent. Keep small bills on hand. Cafés and sit-down restaurants sometimes accept QR payment.

items.title: Go early to avoid selling out
items.text: Legendary noodle spots like Mae Buay open through the afternoon but sell out fast on weekends. Grilled-fish restaurants and riverside spots get packed during evening hours on Saturdays and Sundays. Arriving before peak times or sidestepping the rush means shorter waits.

items.title: English menus are rare
items.text: Most local restaurants here have Thai-only menus and few English speakers. A translation app or pointing at food photos on your phone works well. Café staff in the town center are generally more comfortable with basic English.

items.title: Tipping is not expected
items.text: Roadside restaurants and noodle shops don't have a tipping culture — pay the bill and you're done. At sit-down restaurants or cafés, rounding up or leaving 20–50 THB is a kind gesture but not required.

items.title: Ask the price of fish first
items.text: River fish and grilled prawn dishes at several restaurants are priced by weight or size. Before ordering, ask the price per kilogram or per piece to avoid a surprise at the end. Choose a size that fits your group's appetite.

blocks.title: Plan a full eating day in Prachinburi
blocks.html:
With one day to work with, a solid approach is to start early at Mae Buay Noodles in Ban Sang — the shop opens at 7am and sells out fast on weekends. After that, mid-morning to lunch, loop back toward the city and pick up boat noodles at Nai Tin or Mesa Singha along the old Highway 33 — both are in the Dong Khi Lek strip and starting at 20 THB a bowl, eating multiple rounds is easy.

For the evening, head to Baan Rim Nam for a long riverside meal — grilled prawns and fresh-water fish tom yum with the river breeze. Or if you want grilled snakehead fish as the centrepiece, Khrua Jao Khun Thor is open until 10pm. Close the day with coffee at 93 Degrees Coffee or dessert at Craftel Cafe. For the Kabin Buri side, Khrua A-Ku is the main event there — a large, shaded restaurant that works perfectly for a group.

blocks.text: After a full day of eating, why rush home? Prachinburi has both herb-garden resorts and in-town hotels to choose from. Book a night and wake up to another round of legendary noodles the next morning.

faq.q: Which restaurant is the most famous in Prachinburi?
faq.a: Measured by longevity, Mae Buay Noodles (Ku Na) in Ban Sang has been selling at the same spot for over 58 years — from a tiny wooden stall beside the train tracks to a full restaurant that the whole province knows. For sit-down Thai food, Khrua A-Ku in Kabin Buri is the name that comes up most often in reviews and word-of-mouth recommendations.

faq.q: What are the signature foods of Prachinburi worth trying?
faq.a: First, noodles: the old-recipe pork noodles at Mae Buay and the dense boat noodles of the Dong Khi Lek strip. Then river fish: particularly the straw-grilled snakehead at Khrua Jao Khun Thor and grilled river prawns with fresh-water fish tom yum along the Bang Pakong. Round it out with som tam with fermented fish sauce and grilled chicken at Lek-Was in Nong Juang.

Generally very affordable. Boat noodles start at 20 THB a bowl. Pork noodles run about 50–80 THB. Made-to-order dishes and grilled-fish restaurants average 70–235 THB per dish. Sit-down riverside restaurants like Baan Rim Nam or Khrua A-Ku typically run about 100–250 THB per person — fair considering the freshness of the ingredients.

faq.q: Do Prachinburi restaurants require advance booking?
faq.a: Noodle shops and cafés are walk-in, though expect queues on weekends. For popular spots like Lek-Was som tam in Nong Juang, calling ahead to order saves waiting time. If you're bringing a larger group to a riverside or sit-down restaurant during a holiday period, calling ahead to reserve a table is the easier move.

faq.q: Which restaurants are open in the evening or late at night?
faq.a: Khrua Jao Khun Thor is open until approximately 10pm — the right choice for an evening grilled-fish meal. Riverside restaurants like Baan Rim Nam are also open through the evening at similar hours. Most noodle shops and cafés are daytime operations closing around 4–5pm. Confirm hours before heading out, as they can change.
